_doc: The Caroline fix loop's register: ONE row per SHAPE of customer ask, plus the monitor's thresholds.
Read by scripts/caroline-monitor.py (scripts/caroline_monitor/), checked in PR Validation by
A row records the decision about what KIND of fix a shape gets and where that fix stands. It never
records a conversation: an Intercom id or an inbox link anywhere in this file fails the check.
fix_type: rule (a deterministic answer exists) | tool (a read or an action is missing) | copy (our own
wording causes the ask or makes a wrong promise) | person (genuinely needs one: `person_reason` is
required and the share of threads in person shapes is capped) | refusal (Caroline must not answer the
substance: reason + re-apply path) | none (residual buckets only).
Only rule and tool rows may carry `automation`. A copy fix ships as copy.
status: open | in_progress | shipped | verified | did_not_work | not_planned. Setting `shipped_at`
(YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) + `ref` ARMS the re-measurement: the monitor compares the shape's own rate in the 7
matured days before the fix with the first 7 after it, against every other shape as the control, and
pages if the number did not move. `verified` and `did_not_work` are written from that verdict, never
`fix` on an open row is the missing piece named by the caroline-intent-mining-m1 report (30-day read of
all 4,051 threads, 2026-11-11). It says what kind of fix this is, not how to build it.

monitor._non_human_admin_ids: Caroline and Intercom's Operator bot. Any new bot or AI-queue admin id goes here, or assigning to it would count as a person.
monitor._staffed_team_ids: Team inboxes that people actually work. Empty on purpose: the default team is stamped on every new thread and nobody works it, so a team assignment is not a human assignment until a team is named here.
monitor._page: headline_ceiling_per_week and date_promise_max_per_week are RATCHETS pinned to data/caroline-monitor/baseline.json: the check refuses a value above the baseline, so they only ever come down.

same_step_assignment.why: Caroline sends the hand-off line and the thread stays assigned to herself: a person is promised and nobody is told.
same_step_assignment.fix: Output-guard rule: say a person is coming only when the thread is assigned to a staffed queue in the same step.

human_assignment_by_exception.why: Standing assignment rules put threads on a person's name whether or not that person will answer: assigned hand-offs with no human reply.
human_assignment_by_exception.fix: Remove the standing human-assignment mechanisms; a person is assigned only by an explicit escalation that names its reason.

legal_position.never: State a legal position: what the law requires of Muso, who owns a right, whether something is lawful, what Muso is liable for.
legal_position.reason: A legal position binds Muso and is counsel's to give, not a model's reading of the law.
legal_position.reapply_path: The customer sends the notice or request in writing on the same thread; it is acknowledged with the approved line and answered in writing by the named owner.
legal_position.enforced_by: plugins/intercom/src/caroline-output-guard.ts rule `legal_position`; unanswered legal threads page from scripts/intercom-legal-unanswered-watchdog.py
legal_position.measured_by: outcome class `refused` and `guard_blocked` per shape, on shapes legal_notice and gdpr_erasure

provenance.never: Disclose how a decision was reached: which source was checked, a score, a threshold, a signal, who reviewed it.
provenance.reason: The review's internals are what a forger needs; saying them teaches the next forged document.
provenance.reapply_path: Resubmit the request with supporting documents and a fresh review starts from the beginning (answer-bank line `declined`).
provenance.measured_by: outcome class `refused` on shape declined_why; `guard_blocked` per shape

fraud_label.never: Call a person, a document or an account fraudulent, fake, forged or suspicious, or say it was flagged.
fraud_label.reason: It is an accusation. A wrong one defames a real customer and a right one warns the person it is about.
fraud_label.reapply_path: The customer can send what shows the profile or credit is theirs on the same thread; the decision is made by the named owner and comes back in writing.

date_promise.never: Promise a date, a day count or a time by which something will happen.
date_promise.reason: Nobody owns the clock she would be promising on: of the 873 threads that carried a day-count promise in the 30 days to 2026-11-11, a person replied inside the promised window in 78.
date_promise.reapply_path: State where the request is and what triggers the next message (it arrives on this thread and by email); no clock.
date_promise.residual: The approved claim copy still says `usually within a day` (plugins/intercom/src/answer-bank.ts entries claim_how and timing_claim). It is the whole of what is left; changing approved copy is a copy ruling, not a code fix.

commitments._doc: The promise ledger (scripts/caroline_monitor/commitments.py). When Caroline tells a customer that someone will take it from here, or that it sits in a queue, that sentence is a commitment. A kind says what is being done, what resolves it and WHO OWNS coming back: a job, a rule or a tool, never a person. `owner: null` means nobody can keep this promise yet; it needs `unbacked_reason` and is counted as unbacked. A shape no kind lists is unbacked too. `due_hours` is our own checkpoint for having said something on the thread. It is never told to the customer. A commitment closes only when a message is sent on its own conversation. `priority` is the captain's order (2026-11-11): credit verification first, analytics second, refunds and status third. `request_type` is the request status driver's type (scripts/request_comms/): the driver asks the ledger for the waiting conversation of that type and answers there.

credit_verification.doing: the credit request is being checked against the proof on file
credit_verification.trigger: the request changes state in core (received, verifying, need_you, decided), read hourly by request-comms

analytics.doing: the stream or stats figure the customer questioned is being looked at
analytics.trigger: nothing a job can read yet
analytics.unbacked_reason: no job, rule or tool can read whether an analytics complaint moved. The data-freshness read tool is being designed by intercom-no-human-assignment-k1; name it here when it exists

refund.doing: the refund or charge dispute is with a named human (money is W2: no job decides it)
refund.trigger: the refund ticket changes status in ClickUp
refund.unbacked_reason: request-comms has a refund line but cannot read refunds in production: a ClickUp ticket carries no Muso user id, so the source is unconfigured (scripts/request_comms/driver.py _default_sources)

request_status.doing: the customer asked where a request stands and was not told
request_status.trigger: the request changes state in core, or 48 hours pass with it still open (the waiting line)

claim.doing: the profile claim is being confirmed
claim.trigger: the claim changes state in core, read hourly by request-comms

merge.doing: the profile merge or split is with the catalog queue
merge.trigger: the merge ticket changes status in ClickUp
merge.unbacked_reason: request-comms has a merge line but cannot read merges in production: a ClickUp ticket carries no Muso user id, so the source is unconfigured (scripts/request_comms/driver.py _default_sources)

erasure.doing: the erasure or takedown request is on the GDPR register
erasure.trigger: the register row changes state (scripts/gdpr-pipeline.py), read hourly by request-comms

proof_sent.why: The customer sends proof and Caroline cannot see whether it landed, so she hands off instead of confirming a fact.
proof_sent.fix: Read of `proof_on_file` (built, denied) so the receipt is a checked fact and needs no hand-off line.

proof_what_needed.why: The customer asks what is needed or which credit the mail is about, and she cannot see their open requests.
proof_what_needed.fix: Read of the customer's own open requests by track and role (`credit_verification_check`, `profile_credits_status`). The proof mail's own wording is a second, copy cause.

request_status.why: The customer asks where a request stands and gets the hand-off line or a queue line with no state.
request_status.fix: Read of request state plus the `open_request` fact, so the approved status line can be sent.

claim_start_problem.why: A claim question needs the claim's state and she cannot read it.
claim_start_problem.fix: Read of claim state (`profile_claim_status`, built, denied).

claim_code_added.why: The customer says the code is placed; the daily code check already decides the claim, but she cannot see its result.

credit_add_howto.why: The answer is fixed and approved, and the thread is still handed off.
credit_add_howto.fix: Answer with the approved `credit_how` line; nothing is missing.

request_withdraw_correct.why: The requester wants their own pending request withdrawn or corrected and there is no action for it.
request_withdraw_correct.fix: A tool that withdraws the requester's own pending request.

declined_why.why: Asked why a request was declined, she hands off, though the answer is a refusal she is approved to give.
declined_why.fix: Send the approved `declined` line: the reason she cannot say more, and the way to submit again.

refusal.reason: How a request was reviewed is never disclosed.
refusal.reapply_path: Submit the request again with supporting documents; a fresh review starts from the beginning.

merge_split.why: A merge is judged in shadow and executed by a named human; the customer is told a person is coming and no one is assigned.
merge_split.fix: An executor for the merge verifier's approve verdicts, with an unmerge record.

artist_link.why: The product pre-fills this ask and nothing receives the link the customer supplies.
artist_link.fix: An intake tool that files the supplied link as a link proposal for the presented profile.

credit_wrong.why: A credit is wrong or not theirs; the removal path reports `authority_unavailable` until the core routes deploy.
credit_wrong.fix: The core hide and removal routes (core C1 and C2) behind the existing credit-removal drainer.

track_fix_takedown.why: She files a track-fix ticket and nothing reads that queue.
track_fix_takedown.fix: A drainer for the track-fix tickets she already files.

profile_edit.why: A rename exists as a ledgered action, but only staff can start it.
profile_edit.fix: Owner-initiated rename through the existing ledgered rename action.

claim_conflict.why: Someone else holds the profile the customer says is theirs.
claim_conflict.fix: Assign to the conflicts owner in the same step as the hand-off line.
claim_conflict.person_reason: Deciding which of two people owns a profile is an identity judgement with an accusation inside it; no rule supplies it and Caroline must never label anyone fraudulent.

cancel_subscription.why: Mostly closes today; the residue is handed off when the customer also asks about a charge.
cancel_subscription.fix: Nothing is missing for the cancel itself: answer it, and route the invoice question as billing_question.

refund_dispute.why: The customer wants money back or disputes a charge.
refund_dispute.fix: Assign to the payments owner in the same step as the hand-off line.
refund_dispute.person_reason: A refund is irreversible money and is granted to nobody on any agent path today; the way out is a written refund rule and a capped refund action, which is a spend decision.

billing_question.why: `billing_status` cannot say why a charge happened or failed.
billing_question.fix: Add last payment attempt, retry state, invoice-void state and entitlement to `billing_status`.

plaque_order.why: `order_lookup` returns status only and `order_address_update` refuses every caller while identity verification is off.
plaque_order.fix: Intercom Identity Verification, so the order tools can act for the verified owner.

robot_mail.why: Bounces, helpdesk auto-replies and stray mail get an answer, which starts mail loops and inflates every rate.
robot_mail.fix: Filter non-customer mail on the email channel before any agent turn. For this shape the number that must fall is `answered`.

stats_wrong.why: The customer says a stream count or chart is wrong and she cannot see when each source last updated.
stats_wrong.fix: A data-freshness read: last update per source and any known correction.

account_access.why: Sign-in and email-change asks need the account's state.
account_access.fix: A read of account state: disabled flag, sign-in method, pending email verification.

app_bug.why: She cannot tell a known bug from a new one, or say when it is fixed.
app_bug.fix: A known-issues register she can read and that posts back when an issue is fixed.

gdpr_erasure.why: An erasure or account-deletion request needs an outcome letter.
gdpr_erasure.fix: Send the approved acknowledgement and assign to the erasure owner in the same step.
gdpr_erasure.person_reason: Erasure is a legal process under a legal hold: the pipeline only prepares reversible hide changes, a person merges them, and the outcome letter is a legal statement.

legal_notice.why: A legal notice, takedown demand or security report arrives on the support thread.
legal_notice.fix: Acknowledge and assign to the legal owner in the same step; state no position.
legal_notice.person_reason: Answering a legal notice is stating Muso's legal position, which only a named person may do.

human_request.why: The customer asks for a human and states no need.
human_request.fix: Assign in the same step as the hand-off line.
human_request.person_reason: A plain request for a person is honoured, not argued with; there is no ask for a rule to answer.

api_support.why: API asks need to know whether the workspace has a key and of what type.
api_support.fix: A read of whether a workspace API key exists and its type.

partnership.why: A business or partnership approach lands in support and is handed off to nobody.
partnership.fix: Route to the B2B inbox in the same step. Seen a handful of times a month: not worth more than the route.

product_question.why: Residual bucket: a question the named shapes did not catch. Its growth means a shape is missing from the classifier.

thanks_empty.why: Residual bucket: thanks, a greeting or nothing. No ask to fix.

other.why: Residual bucket: nothing matched. Its size is the discovery input; when it grows, read it and name the shape.
